\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Max Cut Definitions: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCutDefinitions}.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Max Cut Definitions: Results}

\begin{definition}[Valid weighted graph]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsValid}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p073-b005,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p074-b004
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p009-b005}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsValid}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
Let $n\ge 0$ and let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices, with weight
$w(v,u)$ for each ordered pair of vertices. The graph is valid if all weights are
nonnegative, the weights are symmetric in their two vertices, their sum over all ordered
pairs is $1$, and every self-loop has weight $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cut value]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.cutValue}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p034-b005}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p073-b005,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p074-b004
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p009-b005}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.cutValue}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices, and assign each
vertex one of two labels. The cut value of this assignment is the sum of $w(v,u)$ over
all ordered pairs $(v,u)$ whose vertices receive different labels.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Maximum cut value]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.optimum}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p034-b006}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p073-b005,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p074-b004
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p009-b005}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.optimum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.cutValue, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
Let $n\ge 0$ and let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on $n$ vertices. Its optimum cut
value is the supremum of the cut values attained by all assignments of two labels to its
vertices.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Unit vector assignment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsSDPAssignment}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p075-b004}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsSDPAssignment}
\leanok
Let $n\ge 0$, and assign to each of $n$ vertices a vector in $\mathbb R^n$. This
assignment is an SDP assignment if every assigned vector has Euclidean norm $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Semidefinite objective value]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpValue}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p075-b004}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpValue}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
Let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on the vertex set $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and assign
a vector $U_v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ to each vertex. The semidefinite objective value of this
assignment is $\displaystyle \sum_{v,w} w(v,w)\,\frac{1-\langle
U_v,U_w\rangle}{2}$, where the sum ranges over all ordered pairs of vertices.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Semidefinite optimum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpOptimum}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p075-b004}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpOptimum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsSDPAssignment, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpValue, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
Let $G$ be a weighted directed graph on the vertex set $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Its
semidefinite optimum is the supremum of the objective values attained by assignments
$U_v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ that satisfy the semidefinite-program assignment condition.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian hyperplane rounding]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gaussianRounding}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p075-b005,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p076-b002,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p076-b005,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p077-b002
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p009-b007}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gaussianRounding}
\leanok
Let $U_v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ be a vector for each vertex $v\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and
let $g\in\mathbb{R}^n$. The Gaussian rounding of this assignment labels $v$ by true
exactly when $\langle U_v,g\rangle\ge 0$, and by false otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goemans–Williamson constant]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwConstant}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p035-b002,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p051-b001
}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p075-b006,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p076-b004,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p076-b005,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p077-b002
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p009-b007}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwConstant}
\leanok
The Goemans–Williamson constant is the infimum, over $0<\theta\le\pi$, of
$\displaystyle\frac{\theta/\pi}{(1-\cos\theta)/2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goemans–Williamson angle]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwAngle}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p076-b002,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p076-b003,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p076-b005
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p009-b007}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwAngle}
\leanok
The Goemans–Williamson angle is the infimum of the angles $\theta$ satisfying
$0<\theta<\pi$ and $\tan(\theta/2)=\theta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Weighted five-cycle]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycle}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.WeightedDigraph}
On the vertex set $\in 5=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, join two vertices $v,w$ when they are consecutive
modulo $5$, in either order. Give each such ordered pair weight $1/10$ and every other
ordered pair weight $0$; the underlying directed graph has precisely these same ordered
pairs as edges.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Five-cycle SDP vectors]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycleSDP}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.fiveCycleSDP}
\leanok
For each $v\in\in 5$, define a vector in $\bbr^5$ whose first two coordinates are
$\bigl(\cos(4\pi v/5),\sin(4\pi v/5)\bigr)$ and whose remaining three coordinates are
zero.
\end{definition}
